# Template guides

A template is a team: its roles, how work moves through stages, and where it starts (a brief, skills, toolkits, schedules). You pick one on the welcome screen; you can change everything afterwards in Settings.

| Template | For | Work ends as | Needs GitHub |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Software Team](software-team.md) | Building software | Pull requests | Yes |
| [Content Studio](content-studio.md) | Scripts, articles, videos | Files you approve | No |
| [R&D Lab](rd-lab.md) | Questions answered by experiment | A report you approve | No |
| [Start with a lead](lead-only.md) | Anything; the lead hires | Files the lead reviews | No |
| [Newsletter desk](newsletter-desk.md) (gallery) | A weekly newsletter | An issue you sign off | No |
| [Market research](market-research.md) (gallery) | Sourced answers to market questions | A report you approve | No |
| [Website builder](website-builder.md) (gallery) | Websites and web apps, browser-tested | Pull requests | Yes |

The gallery ones aren't built in: install them from **Settings → Templates → Gallery**, or **Install a template** on the welcome screen. See [Sharing templates](../sharing-templates.md) to publish your own.

Every guide assumes HQ is installed and running (`npx yacc-hq` in your project's folder, see [Getting started](../getting-started.md)). Agents can run in Docker Sandboxes or, on any machine, in **Local mode** with Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI.
